Three series of calculations are considered, with the incident-shock normal Mach number fixed at 2, 4 and 8, respectively. Within each series, the incidence angle is reduced while the normal strength of the incident shock remains unchanged. The decrease in angle primarily results in a longer non-equilibrium region of shock-wave interaction. Over the parameter range considered, the density-transition width along the plane of symmetry is approximately inversely proportional to the sine of the incidence angle. Increasing the normal Mach number enhances temperature anisotropy, the local temperature overshoot relative to the equilibrium downstream state, and the streamwise-velocity undershoot.

papers.title: Open CDLM: A Benchmark and Library for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Reliable comparisons of continuous diffusion language models (CDLMs) require evaluating both model fit and the distribution of generated text. Two common practices leave this goal only partially addressed. Likelihood-based evaluation often reports a variational upper bound on discrete negative log-likelihood, whose slack can confound comparisons. Generated-sample-based evaluation commonly combines generative perplexity with within-sequence unigram entropy; both scores can remain favorable even when a sampler produces the same text on every draw. We introduce \textbf{Open CDLM}, a benchmark for evaluating CDLMs and their samplers, and describe the design of an accompanying open-source library to support reproducible comparisons. For likelihood-based evaluation, we clarify which comparisons of model fit are supported by reported perplexity bounds and how those conclusions depend on the evaluation procedure. For sample-based evaluation, we use \textit{Kernel Text Discrepancy} (\textbf{KTD}) to compare collections of generated and real texts, alongside diagnostics for diversity, validity, and coverage. In controlled OpenWebText experiments, replacing a collection of texts with copies of a single selected passage improves both conventional generation scores. MAUVE detects the resulting collapse, and its response to other perturbations depends on the text representation and the type of perturbation. This work marks the beginning of Open CDLM as an open-source project for CDLM research. We will maintain and extend the library over time and welcome contributions from the community.

papers.title: geodesiq: a Python package for geometric diabatic-adiabatic optimal state transfer
papers.abstract: We introduce the geodesiq Python package, which implements a geometric framework for shaping control pulses that achieve high-fidelity state transfer in multilevel quantum systems. The underlying method combines adiabatic and diabatic control into a single metric, suppressing unwanted excitations while allowing selected diabatic passages. Finding the pulse thereby reduces to solving a single first-order ordinary differential equation. We explain how to use geodesiq and illustrate its use explicitly with Landau-Zener transitions, spin-qubit initialization, adiabatic many-body ground-state preparation, and a diabatic-adiabatic transfer in a four-level system.

papers.title: Nutrient limitation drives Turing instabilities in cross-feeding microbial communities
papers.abstract: Microbial communities are shaped by metabolic interactions, often in the form of cross-feeding in which microbes exchange metabolites via diffusion through the environment. We show here that the diffusion of cross-fed metabolites generically leads to a Turing instability in resource-poor environments, driven by the feedback between local metabolite availability and cell growth. A coarse-grained model of community biomass identifies the few dimensionless parameters that control the instability, most notably the ratio of environmental energy supply to cellular maintenance costs. We find that the detailed topology of the metabolic interaction network can be coarse-grained into a single effective parameter to quantitatively characterise the instability. Beyond the onset of the instability, the community forms compact aggregates whose merger is prevented by a competition for shared resources. Overall, our results demonstrate how spatial structure can arise as an inevitable consequence of metabolic interactions in a microbial community.

papers.title: Standard-Anchored Delegation in Teachers' Use of Generative AI
papers.abstract: Teachers who use generative AI must decide which parts of their work to hand over, while they remain accountable for what reaches students. We studied these decisions in Punjab, Pakistan, through a qualitatively driven mixed-methods study. We interviewed 13 teachers from government, private, NGO and vocational institutions, four administrators and one student, and coded each teacher's position on twelve educational tasks. Nine teachers accepted AI drafts or substantial assistance with lesson planning, but none accepted AI-drafted learning objectives, and eleven did not use AI to encourage or emotionally support students. Teachers who would accept AI marking required that the model be given a rubric or marking criteria. Building on assessment research and HCI work on verifiability, we call this pattern standard-anchored delegation: teachers handed a component of a task to AI when a standard outside the model, such as a textbook or rubric, defined a correct output and the teacher could apply that standard to the result. Having a standard was not always enough. Several government-school teachers did not use AI to mark quizzes even though the quizzes had answer keys, because they expected students to look for evidence of the teacher's effort. Checking AI output required subject knowledge and time, and private schools gave teachers more support for this than government schools did. Participants also read disclosure of AI use as a statement about whether the teacher had reviewed the work. We propose that teacher-facing AI tools ask for the relevant standard before generating and show each output beside it, and that schools account for the time that checking takes.

papers.title: Annular Terahertz Near-Field of a Breathing Charged Vortex
papers.abstract: We study the radial electric field around a singly quantized vortex in a charged BCS superconductor, when the Higgs amplitude mode is driven by a uniform terahertz (THz) electromagnetic pulse. In a local-density approximation the pairing gap vanishes on the vortex axis at all times, so the particle density on the axis cannot oscillate, whereas the curvature of the density profile around the axis does. Starting from the electrostatic-lens formalism of our previous work, we show that this converts the electrically neutral Higgs oscillation into an alternating radial electric field that vanishes on the axis. When the electrostatic screening length is much shorter than the vortex core, we obtain the field in closed form: it has a ring-shaped profile, with a maximum at a distance of the order of the coherence length from the axis, and the Higgs drive modulates it by a fraction $2\eta$, where $\eta$ is the relative oscillation of the gap. For niobium nitride and $\eta=0.1$ the static field of the vortex is about $140$~V/m and its modulation about $30$~V/m, independently of the carrier density and of the dielectric constant. We also discuss how the thermodynamic factor entering the field changes toward the BCS-BEC crossover.

papers.title: Squarefree powers of simplicial forests
papers.abstract: The highest nonzero squarefree power of an edge ideal always has linear quotients, whereas this property can fail even for the facet ideal of a pure two-dimensional simplicial tree. This raises the question of which combinatorial conditions ensure linear quotients beyond the graph case. We characterize the squarefree powers of facet ideals of pure simplicial forests that have linear quotients, showing that this property is equivalent to having a linear resolution or being linearly related. We also investigate the corresponding question for undirected path ideals of forests. Here the highest nonzero squarefree power always has linear quotients for $3$-path ideals, whereas the analogous assertion fails for $4$-path ideals of trees.

papers.title: Blowing star formation away in AGN Hosts (BAH) - VI. Warm Molecular Outflows Driven by the Low-Luminosity AGN in NGC 3884
papers.abstract: We use the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI) Medium Resolution Spectrograph (MRS) to investigate the warm molecular and low ionization gas outflows driven by the low-luminosity Active Galactic Nucleus (AGN) in NGC 3884. By decomposing the emission-line profiles into multiple Gaussian components, we detect both ionized and warm molecular outflows, traced by [Ar ii] 6.99 um and H2 0-0 S(5), respectively. The ionized and warm molecular components both extend to similar distances from the nucleus, reaching approximately ~1.2 kpc. In addition to an outflow component, we detect a double narrow emission component in both ionized and molecular lines, clearly observed along the minor axis with similar amplitudes, while their intensity ratio varies systematically along the major axis. Both components exhibit similar line widths and centroid velocity distributions, indicating that they are not associated with outflows, but instead arise from gas in the galaxy disk. We estimate that the outflow injects momentum into the interstellar medium (ISM) at a rate corresponding to ~0.015 percent of the AGN bolometric luminosity, consistent with a radiation-driven origin. Assuming a constant outflow rate, the gas reservoir would be depleted on a timescale of ~26 Myr, potentially suppressing nuclear star formation in the host galaxy.

papers.title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
papers.abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects in an image and predict the relationships between them. The standard PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet settings show how much performance drops without ground-truth boxes and labels, but not where or why a model fails. Knowing this would allow fixing a model where it fails, without retraining. We propose RoHa-SGG (Root-cause-guided Harness optimization for SGG), which extends agentic harness optimization to SGG. It optimizes the harness, the inference code around a frozen SGG model. RoHa-SGG has two main LLM agents. A root-cause analysis (RCA) agent finds the components where the model fails and diagnoses why, and a proposer agent searches for a harness that fixes these causes. We evaluate RoHa-SGG on Visual Genome and PSG with representative two-stage, one-stage, and multimodal-LLM SGG models. The analysis shows that the components where ground-truth triplets are lost differ across models and datasets. RoHa-SGG improves every metric on all five model-dataset combinations. Graph-constrained R@100 and mR@100 rise by up to 15.8 and 26.4 points for the multimodal LLM and by up to 3.6 and 10.1 points for the two-stage and one-stage models. With root-cause guidance, the harness search reaches the final score of an unguided search up to three times faster.

papers.title: Rigidity and nonrigidity for interval translation maps
papers.abstract: Almost every infinite-type interval translation map in the Bruin--Troubetzkoy family, and in Bruin's family with any fixed number of branches, is rigid for its invariant probability, where typicality is understood with respect to the intrinsic induction parameter measure. We prove this by exhibiting explicit repeated-word blocks in the induction and showing that their cylinders recur. In the opposite direction, we give a sufficient condition for nonrigidity of a primitive aperiodic substitution: the existence of a rational periodic vector of its incidence matrix in the return-word space whose coordinate sum is nonzero. The proof gives a uniform positive lower bound for symbol discrepancies at all sufficiently large times. For self-similar Bruin maps with primitive period substitution, the same condition also implies weak mixing. We apply the nonrigidity condition to an explicit self-similar infinite-type Bruin map on eight intervals, specifying its algebraic parameters and verifying its return words.

papers.title: Modelling scintillation in Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abstract:
Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs) are bright, ms-duration, extragalactic radio transients. Propagation through inhomogeneities in the ionised medium produces scintillation, observed as frequency-dependent intensity variations in their spectra, with bright patches, called scintles. The characteristic scintillation bandwidth probes scattering material along the line of sight. Measuring this scale can be challenging when the observing bandwidth of the burst spectra contains a few scintles. We study the uncertainties associated with recovering $
u_s$ from frequency autocorrelation functions (ACFs) under finite-bandwidth conditions. We examine the recovery of $
u_s$ from individual ACFs and investigate if averaging multiple independent ACFs provides a more robust measurement. Using simulations, we reproduce observational conditions to investigate the modelling of scintillation in ACFs and the associated measurement uncertainties. We use these simulations to test the finite scintle error (FSE) prescription and assess its applicability to real observations. We test the resulting modelling framework on Effelsberg Ultra Broad Band receiver observations of the repeating FRB 20240114A. As the number of scintles decreases, individual ACFs develop fluctuations that deviate from the expected Lorentzian profile. This results in increased scatter in the recovered $
u_s$ and a less reliable FSE prescription. Averaging multiple independent ACFs mitigates these effects and improves the recovery of $
u_s$ in the low-scintle regime. Our results provide a framework for ACF modelling and uncertainty estimation in FRBs. For individual bursts, the FSE is effective with sufficient scintles; we find $\eta = 0.055$ more suitable for FRB analysis and update the FSE accordingly. For repeaters, averaging multiple ACFs and bootstrap resampling improve the recovery and uncertainty estimation of $
u_s$.

papers.title: Coerciveness for complex Hessian type equations
papers.abstract: We study complex Hessian type equations associated with right-Noetherian polynomials on compact K\"ahler manifolds of complex dimension $n$. For two such polynomials of the same degree $2\le d\le n$ in strict proper position, we prove that under the integrability condition and the assumption that the admissible space $\mathcal{H}_2$ is non-empty, smooth admissible solvability for $f_1$, the $d_1$-coerciveness of the associated variational functional $J_1$ on normalized potentials, and the numerical criterion for $f_1$ are equivalent to each other. This extends the existence-coerciveness correspondence of Chen-Ghosh-Wang to the lower-degree setting under weaker polynomial conditions.

papers.title: PennyGS: Full Resolution 3DGS Training in Minutes on Consumer GPUs
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting is increasingly fed by high-resolution captures from commodity devices, yet training still happens at reduced resolution with research-grade GPUs. We present PennyGS, a method to achieve full-resolution (4K) training of 3DGS on consumer GPUs by improving the efficiency of every stage of a training step. Improvements include a leaner splat with flat RGB color and a directional cone opacity, fused projection and key emission, forward rasterization optimizations with strided pixel sampling, an approximate tile SSIM loss, a warp-per-splat backward rasterization, and a fused backward projection and sparse Adam step. At the standard 30k-step budget, PennyGS is the fastest of 10 methods on Mip-NeRF 360 and Tanks&Temples 4K on all four GPUs at competitive quality, at least 3.9x faster than the quickest of the others, while peaking below 2 GB of GPU memory. On an RTX 3060, a full-resolution Mip-NeRF 360 scene trains in 6m 25s, faster than any other method trains it on an RTX 4090.

papers.title: Adaptive-Optics-Aware Uplink and Downlink Analysis of Ground-to-HAPS FSO Links
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present an adaptive optics (AO)-aware analytical framework for ground-to- high-altitude platform station (HAPS) free-space optical (FSO) links considering both uplink (UL) and downlink (DL) transmission. The proposed model combines atmospheric attenuation, Exponentiated Weibull (EW) turbulence, Beckmann-type pointing error (PE), and field-of-view (FoV)-limited angle-of-arrival (AOA) loss. Adaptive optics correction (AOC) is incorporated through the number of corrected modes, allowing the impact of partial and stronger wavefront compensation to be directly reflected in the channel statistics. Analytical and numerically tractable expressions are derived for the outage probability (OP), average bit-error rate (BER), and an ergodic achievable-rate lower bound (EALB) optical channel. High signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) approximations are also developed, showing that AOA/FoV blocking introduces irreducible OP and BER floors, while the decaying nonblocked component is governed by the small-channel-gain behavior of the turbulence and PE distributions. Numerical results demonstrate that the DL generally outperforms the UL because of the direction-dependent interaction with near-ground turbulence. The results also show that increasing the number of AOC modes improves OP, BER, and the EALB, although the improvement gradually saturates. The effects of average SNR, HAPS altitude, zenith angle, beam waist, boresight error, and receiver FoV are further investigated to provide practical design insight for AO-assisted ground-to-HAPS FSO systems.

papers.title: Actively stabilized Fabry-P\'erot notch filters for correlated photons from cold two-level atoms
papers.abstract: We report two actively stabilized Fabry-P\'erot cavities operated as reflection-mode notch filters for biphotons generated by spontaneous four-wave mixing in a cold two-level atomic ensemble. In this source, elastic scattering at the excitation frequency increases the single-detector count rates and the accidental-coincidence background, thereby limiting the observed nonclassical correlations. One cavity is placed in each photon-collection mode. An acousto-optic modulator frequency-dithers an auxiliary field, and synchronous demodulation of the transmitted power provides the locking discriminator. Light resonant with the auxiliary field is transmitted, whereas the detuned components are reflected toward the photon detectors. By tuning the auxiliary field to the same frequency as the excitation field, we filter these components and direct a larger portion of the quantum-correlated sidebands to the detection. The cavities have linewidths of approximately 2 MHz and remain locked for longer than a typical correlation acquisition. The measured Cauchy-Schwarz parameter exceeds unity in both configurations, with a higher central value with filtering ($\overline{R} = 4.15 \pm 0.93$) than without ($\overline{R} = 2.33 \pm 0.20$). This architecture provides actively stabilized rejection of a narrow spectral interval, simultaneously, for two fields detected in different directions. Filter performance could be further improved by adjusting the cavity linewidth to better match the spectral width of the central component and by reducing losses in the filters.

papers.title: The First Adolescent Super-Earth-Sized Multi-Planet System Around an M Dwarf: TOI-2079
papers.abstract: We identify two planets in close-in orbits around the M-type star TOI-2079 as the first super-Earth-sized planets orbiting a multi-planet M dwarf with a well-determined age of $1$-$2$\,Gyr. The interior planet, TOI-2079 b, has an orbital period of $1.49232359^{+0.00000099}_{-0.00000086}$ d, and the outer planet, TOI-2079 c, has an orbital period of $9.3174523\pm0.0000098$ d. The host star characterization is based on spectroscopic observations, which classify it from an M1.5 to an M3.5 dwarf with an effective temperature of $3695\pm77$ K. Further analysis determined TOI-2079's rotation period to be $17.33^{+0.29}_{-0.28}$ d. Multiple ground-based follow-up observations, combined with a state-of-the-art validation procedure, allow us to rule out possible astrophysical false-positive scenarios and validate the planetary nature of both objects. We find that the inner planet has a radius of $1.320\pm0.050 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 867\pm27$ K, while the outer planet has $R_{\rm p} = 1.671\pm0.051 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 473\pm15$ K.

papers.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks
papers.abstract: While vision-language models (VLMs) currently obtain notable results for highly-studied languages, e.g. English, they exhibit significant performance drops in certain low-resource languages, especially due to the lack of annotated datasets. To this end, we propose PaMuk-Bench, a novel parallel multilingual multitask benchmark for vision-language tasks. Our benchmark includes a set of over 10K curated English prompts that are translated into six languages: Arabic, Danish, French, Hindi, Italian, Romanian. Parallel translations, which are obtained via a semi-automatic process, along with accompanying generated and retrieved images enable the comparative development and evaluation of VLMs across a wide range of tasks: text-to-image generation, image captioning, content-based image retrieval, image generation difficulty estimation, image retrieval difficulty estimation. We empirically show that zero-shot English and multilingual pre-trained VLMs compare consistently worse than their fine-tuned counterparts, confirming that PaMuk-Bench is a valuable resource that can drastically reduce the language gap across a variety of VLM architectures and tasks. PaMuk-Bench is available at https://github.com/ghesil/pamuk_bench.

papers.title: Approximating technique for the solution to the ${H}^{\infty}$ -optimal control problem
papers.abstract: This paper continues the results published in [G. Marinoschi, Appl. Math. Optimiz. 94:44, 1-29, 2026], by presenting an approximating method of calculating the solution to the $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem, which solves the robust stabilization of a system by a feedback controller, and to the associated Riccati equation. This method generates a sequence of infinite dimensional systems approximating the original system and the solution to the approximating $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem is proved to converge to the solution of the original $H^{\infty }$-optimal control problem. An example for calculating the solution to the Riccati equation and the feedback controller is provided at the end.

papers.title: Additive cubes are avoidable by a non-uniform morphism of length $6$ over $\{0,a,b\}$ (with $b \ge 4$ and $\gcd(a,b) = 1$)
papers.abstract: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over every ternary alphabet $\{0, a, b\}$ with $1 \le a < b$, $\gcd(a, b) = 1$, and $b \ge 4$, thereby solving and extending Rao's~(2015) conjecture from $b \ge 6$ down to $b \ge 4$. Our construction applies a single dual pair of parameterized non-uniform morphisms of image length at most~$6$ to the additive-cube-free word $\mathbf{w}$ of Cassaigne et al.~(2014). For $b \ge 10$, we prove that every additive square in the image is an abelian square, reducing additive cubes to abelian cubes; the absence of abelian cubes and the $24$ finite cases with $4 \le b \le 9$ are then certified via the finite-graph method of Jamet and Rosenfeld~(2026).

papers.title: Probing Compressed Dark Sectors at a Muon Collider through Dilepton Signatures and Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The inert doublet model (IDM), a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM), provides a scalar dark matter (DM) candidate that belongs to the additional Higgs doublet. The model faces challenges in achieving the correct relic abundance for compressed spectra and DM masses in the high-mass range. In this work we investigate the prospects of detecting dark matter candidates at future high-energy muon colliders. Focusing on the process $\mu^+ \mu^- \to AH$ with subsequent decay $A \to H Z^*$ and $Z^* \to \ell^+\ell^-$, we explore the sensitivity of machine learning techniques, specifically Boosted Decision Trees (BDT) and XGBoost, to distinguish the signal from Standard Model backgrounds. We demonstrate that the combination of advanced multivariate analysis with high-luminosity muon collisions enhances the discovery potential for inert scalars in compressed mass spectra scenarios.

papers.title: EchoAlign: Echocardiography foundation model with multilevel report alignment
papers.abstract: Echocardiography assesses the structure and function of the heart. Cardiologists read each study across several standard views and report the findings visible in those views by cardiac structure. AI foundation models can learn to analyze these studies from clinical reports, reducing annotation burden and supporting clinical interpretation. However, existing models are trained by pairing each video with the full clinical report, including structures and findings its view does not show. This mismatch lets a model associate a finding with incidental or spurious signals rather than its visual evidence, which limits accuracy, anatomical grounding and clinical trust. Here we introduce EchoAlign, a vision-language foundation model developed on 2.87 million echocardiographic videos and images from 159 clinical centers. EchoAlign aligns each cardiac structure, video and study with its report text, and a visibility matrix restricts supervision to the views that actually depict each structure. We compare it with five public foundation models on 0.47 million test videos across ten unseen external datasets from more than 25 clinical centers. EchoAlign achieves the highest mean AUROC of 0.890 (95% CI, 0.881 to 0.897) for classification and the highest mean quadratic weighted kappa of 0.530 (95% CI, 0.511 to 0.544) for severity grading. Across 62 clinical findings, EchoAlign provides one model that detects findings, grades their severity, estimates measurements and segments cardiac structures.

papers.title: PhiJEPA: Denoising Latent Predictions for Visual Representation Learning
papers.abstract: Can a predictor trained to infer hidden image regions still help a world model plan when part of an object disappears from view and the visible context is blurred? We introduce PhiJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture that adapts PhiNet's two-stage prediction to masked Transformers. From sparse, photometrically corrupted context, a Transformer block predicts hidden tokens of an independently corrupted teacher view. A token-wise MLP then maps these predictions to clean teacher tokens. Controlled ablations show that the combined objective improves dense features over the tested one-stage alternatives. Pre-trained on ImageNet-1K with $5.6\times10^{19}$ training FLOPs, PhiJEPA achieves 69.3 mIoU on linear PASCAL VOC segmentation, exceeding the evaluated I-JEPA and DSeq-JEPA checkpoints in segmentation accuracy, with 25\% fewer training FLOPs than I-JEPA. It also improves hidden-region segmentation over Simple I-JEPA (49.1 vs.\ 44.3 mIoU). As an application, we use the frozen encoder in DINO-WM on PushT, and reuse the pre-training predictor, which JEPAs usually discard, to complete occluded tokens without fine-tuning. In open-loop planning with simultaneous object occlusion and Gaussian blur ($\sigma=2$ pixels), predictor completion raises success from 33\% to 65\%, compared with 25\% for Simple I-JEPA with its predictor and 40\% for iBOT with pixel inpainting. Together, these results support two-stage latent prediction as an efficient approach to learning visual representations that remain useful under photometric degradation and support completion under partial observation.

papers.title: Beyond a Single Human Demonstration: Learning from Scored Trajectory Alternatives for End-to-End Driving
papers.abstract: Human driving logs record only one trajectory per scene, leaving other feasible driving choices without explicit trajectory targets or quality labels. This limits supervision for end-to-end planners that generate and refine multiple candidate trajectories. Meanwhile, conditioning refinement on a large vision-language model adds substantial online inference cost. We propose DriveSTA, which extends autoregressive proposal generation and proposal-conditioned residual flow refinement with scored trajectory alternatives. For each training scene, we generate alternatives offline through smooth deformations of the recorded trajectory and evaluate their simulated execution against logged traffic. Diverse, high-quality alternatives supervise distinct proposals and define residual targets for quality-guided denoising, while candidates spanning the full score range train a scorer to assess driving quality. A shared joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), adapted through masked video-feature prediction, encodes observed frames once and provides temporal context for both refinement and scoring. On NAVSIM v1 Navtest, DriveSTA ranks first among the compared planners trained on NAVSIM data alone. With expanded training data, DriveSTA-Scale achieves state-of-the-art results among the compared methods on Navtest and closed-loop HUGSIM, while reducing mean planner forward-pass latency by 73% relative to ChainFlow-VLA in matched evaluations.

papers.title: Deep Cross-Division Network for Product-and-Ratio Feature Interactions in Industrial Ranking
papers.abstract: Learning effective feature interactions is essential for industrial recommender systems. DCN and DCNv2 efficiently automate polynomial feature crossing. However, their cross layers construct interactions using only non-negative integer powers of the input features, with the maximum degree controlled by network depth. Consequently, they cannot directly represent the reciprocal terms required for ratios, rates, and normalized counts unless such features are explicitly provided as inputs. We introduce DCDN, a Deep Cross-Division Network that augments a DCNv2-style cross layer with a division branch. DCDN jointly learns product, ratio, and mixed product-ratio interactions. We characterize the representable interactions as multivariate Laurent polynomials and show that a $K$-layer DCDN generates Laurent monomials of $\ell_1$-order up to $K+1$, with signed degree between $-K$ and $K+1$. We evaluate DCDN against a production-optimized neural-ranking baseline built around DCNv2 and supplied with manually engineered ratio features. Replacing the DCNv2 block with DCDN allowed us to eliminate the entire class of manually engineered ratio features from the model input, reducing the number of input features by $40.1\%$. DCDN is deployed in the production ranking stack of a major short-video service. In a live A/B test on this service, DCDN increased likes by $3.25\%$, shares by $16.26\%$, total view time (TVT) by $0.33\%$, and clicks to open fullscreen by $0.38\%$; all changes were statistically significant. The number of shown videos decreased slightly ($-0.24\%$). These results demonstrate that DCDN can improve user engagement while eliminating reliance on manually engineered ratio features. Our code is publicly released at https://github.com/rw404/DCDN.

papers.title: Ego4Gen: Generating Geometry-Grounded Motion Tokens as a World-Action Interface
papers.abstract: We present Ego4Gen (Egocentric 4D Future Generation), a world model for 4D future generation in robotic manipu lation. Given a single egocentric image and a text prompt, Ego4Gen jointly generates temporally aligned RGB frames, dense point maps, and dense scene flow, explicitly pre dicting the evolution of scene appearance, spatial struc ture, and motion. Built on Cosmos3-Nano, Ego4Gen ex tends the pretrained generative backbone through modality routed LoRA and asymmetric attention, using geometric pseudo-labels from MotionCrafter to learn to predict future geometry and motion latents. These latents can either be decoded into explicit 3D structure and motion or mapped to robot actions. To this end, we also introduce FlowIn verse, a lightweight inverse dynamics network trained in two stages to translate predicted 4D latents into robot ac tions. Experiments show that these geometry and motion latents outperform the evaluated latent-action and video latent baselines in out-of-distribution settings. Closed loop policy evaluations further demonstrate their utility for translating predicted 4D futures into robot control. To gether, these results support geometry-grounded motion to kens as a world-action interface, connecting 4D future gen eration with robotic manipulation and suggesting a path to ward reduced reliance on action-labeled data.

papers.title: PGS-PCQA: Perceptually Gated Synthetic Supervision for No-Reference Point Cloud Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: Existing no-reference point cloud quality assessment (NR-PCQA) methods perform well within individual datasets but generalize poorly across datasets. We identify insufficient distortion coverage in training data as a key cause: on unseen distortion types, models rank severity levels near chance or even in reverse. We propose perceptually gated synthetic supervision for no-reference point cloud quality assessment (PGS-PCQA), an NR-PCQA model trained with synthetic distortion ranking. It builds a synthetic distortion bank from source reference point clouds and uses within-type severity ranking as supervision in addition to the source mean opinion scores (MOS), requiring no subjective scores for the synthetic samples. Since higher severity does not always mean lower perceived quality, a perceptual gate softens the ranking targets of pairs with small perceptual differences in rendered views. The synthetic supervision is used only during training and needs no target-domain data. In a single training run on SJTU-PCQA, PGS-PCQA achieves Spearman rank correlation coefficients (SRCCs) of 0.709 on WPC and 0.751 on BASICS. The corresponding published DSP-PCQA scores are 0.595 and 0.723. Under reference-disjoint cross-validation, PGS-PCQA achieves SRCCs of 0.955 on SJTU-PCQA, 0.934 on WPC, 0.906 on BASICS, and 0.791 on LS-PCQA Part I. In the exclusion experiment, the reported scores for the reduced synthetic bank represent 58-65% of the full-bank SRCC gain relative to training without the bank. Code is available at https://github.com/Fan-QY/PGS-PCQA.

papers.title: Breaking the Barrier of Hard Samples: A Data-Centric Approach to Synthetic Data for Medical Tasks
papers.abstract: Data scarcity and quality issues remain significant barriers to developing robust predictive models in medical research. Traditional reliance on real-world data often leads to biased models with poor generalizability across diverse patient populations. Synthetic data generation has emerged as a promising solution, yet challenges related to these samples' representativeness and effective utilization persist. This paper introduces Profile2Gen, a novel data-centric framework designed to guide the generation and refinement of synthetic data, focusing on addressing hard-to-learn samples in regression tasks. We conducted approximately 18,000 experiments to validate its effectiveness across six medical datasets, utilizing seven state-of-the-art generative models. Results demonstrate that refined synthetic samples can reduce predictive errors and enhance model reliability. Additionally, we generalize the DataIQ framework to support regression tasks, enabling its application in broader contexts. Statistical analyses confirm that our approach achieves equal or superior performance compared to models trained exclusively on real data.

papers.title: Operative Representation of Quasi-Arithmetic Means, Complex Branch Structure, and Covariant Commutator Defects in Iterated Logarithmic Operation Hierarchies
papers.abstract: We investigate the bidirectional family of commutative binary operations $\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[x,y] = f_a^{(-m)}(f_a^{(m)}(x) + f_a^{(m)}(y))$ ($m \in \mathbb{Z}$) generated by iterating the scaled logarithmic Cauchy isomorphism $f_a(z) = \frac{1}{a}\ln(z)$ ($a > 0$). Our analysis focuses on three structural properties of this hierarchy. First, we show that for all $m \ge -1$ the associated quasi-arithmetic Kolmogorov-Nagumo means $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x})$ admit a closed two-stage operative representation $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathrm{Op}_{m+1}^{(a)}[\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[\mathbf{x}], N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n)]$ with normalization factor $N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n) = f_a^{(-m)}(1/n)$, and prove that this internal operative normalizability via a distributive adjacent level characterizes logarithmic generators among continuously conjugated group operations. Second, we show that for $m \le -2$ and $n \ge 2$ the normalization factor leaves the positive real domain $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, motivating the analytic continuation onto the Riemann surface of the logarithm; there, a fundamental dichotomy emerges between the internal branch-index invariance of $\mathrm{Op}_{-1}^{(a)}$ and the associativity defect $\omega(x,z)$ generated by $\mathrm{Op}_2^{(a)}$. Third, for arbitrary levels $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ and sample sizes $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we derive the general covariance pushforward theorem $\mathrm{Sp}_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = f_a^{(-m)}(\mathrm{Cov}(f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{x}), f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{y})))$ governing the commutator defect between mean formation and the adjacent operation.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Continuous-Time Depth Learning and Ego-Motion Estimation from Asynchronous Events
papers.abstract: Event cameras register brightness changes pixel by pixel with microsecond precision, whereas the dense depth that could supervise them is costly to acquire and exists only at isolated instants. Condensing the stream into frames eases learning, but at the expense of the very timing that sets event sensing apart. We propose a self-supervised approach in which each event is assigned its own depth in continuous time, and the camera motion is recovered from the same observations. Supervision arises from geometry: lifted into 3D by its predicted depth and displaced by the camera motion at the instant it fired, an event should coincide with others produced by the same edge, so any misalignment exposes an error in depth or motion. Differentiable rendering then turns these per-event estimates into dense depth maps at target times within each window, faithful to the events behind them. On MVSEC, the approach outperforms prior event-only self-supervised methods in most sequences and depth ranges, with the widest margins at night, and recovers camera rotation more accurately than an earlier unsupervised event-based method. Ablations isolate the roles of local spatiotemporal context, the temporal backbone, and the alignment objective. These results position motion-compensated event alignment as a principled source of supervision for continuous-time depth and ego-motion estimation.

papers.title: Hard X-ray spectroscopy of a short-period asynchronous polar: IGR J19552+0044
papers.abstract: IGR J19552+0044 is an asynchronous polar with a beat modulation of $\approx2$ days due to $\approx3$% spin-orbit asynchronism. We present the first hard X-ray properties of this system using a NuSTAR observation. Spectral modeling yields a shock temperature of $kT_{\rm s}=44.50^{+3.60}_{-3.29}$ keV, implying a white dwarf mass of $M_{\rm WD}\geq 0.85\,M_\odot$. We infer an average accretion rate of $\dot{M}\sim 3.0\times 10^{-11}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, consistent with expectations for short-period systems (orbital period $<2$ h). Even at this low accretion rate, we detect a significant Compton reflection component that gives a shock height of $H\sim 0.3\,R_{\rm WD}$. Time-resolved spectroscopy of the observation, covering $\approx61$% of a beat cycle, reveals a variation in $\dot{M}$ by a factor of $\sim 4.5$, providing X-ray evidence for the magnetic valve mechanism. Despite the large variations in $\dot{M}$, no significant change in shock temperature is observed. This weak thermal response constrains the shock structure on the white dwarf surface, favoring a shock height that remains approximately constant as $\dot{M}$ changes, potentially due to variations in the fractional accretion area $f$.

papers.title: Classical simulability and hardware diagnostics for QAOA on geographic coverage benchmarks
papers.abstract: Quantum-optimization benchmarks can show reduced energy while concealing local loss of weighted covariance. We combine encoding checks with exact structural references to select informative circuit diagnostics for static geographic coverage instances. The executed 24-qubit surrogate has infeasible ground states, whereas a faithful 51-qubit slack encoding preserves its 13 support-graph components and remains exactly simulable blockwise. At the executed angles, the total ideal optimum probability is $5.47\times10^{-20}$, making optimum counts uninformative at the executed budget of $10^5$ shots. A product distribution with the measured bit marginals accounts for about $90\%$ of the observed energy reduction. In three fixed-circuit jobs, the global weighted-covariance ratio is approximately $0.50$, while a five-variable block has ratios between $0.12$ and $0.28$ and contributes only $3.7\%$ of the ideal global denominator. Simultaneous bands resolve its deficit relative to the global ratio under an exploratory conditional counting model. The exact block reference thus reveals a local discrepancy concealed by the aggregate, without identifying an error mechanism or establishing device stability. The procedure links benchmark structure to the resolution and limitations of its observables.

papers.title: How Many Bytes Has a BPE Model Seen? Estimating Byte-Token Exposure in Pretraining from Corpus Statistics and Embedding Norms
papers.abstract: Byte-level BPE vocabularies retain 256 single-byte fallback tokens. When converting such a model into a pure byte-level model, these tokens provide the starting embeddings. How much training have they received? We estimate byte-token exposure in Qwen3.8 using two independent routes. First, we tokenize 540 MB of public corpora covering 40 domains and 33 languages, then combine per-domain token shares with assumed pretraining mixtures. Single-byte tokens account for 13 to 36% of tokens, mostly ASCII; genuine UTF-8 fallback bytes (0x80-0xFF) account for 0.15 to 0.27% under mainstream mixtures, or about 2 billion occurrences per trillion pretraining tokens. Fallback rates vary by four orders of magnitude across languages, reflecting how well each script is covered by the vocabulary. Second, we analyze embedding and output-matrix row norms for four open models, using untrained padding rows as a zero-exposure baseline and ordinary tokens with known frequencies for calibration. In all four models, the 13 bytes that cannot occur in valid UTF-8 remain at initialization, while every legal high byte lies in a high-frequency band. For Qwen3.8, the norm-based estimate agrees with the corpus estimate within a factor of four. The norm-frequency relation eventually folds, so inversion is useful only as a model-specific, order-of-magnitude estimate. No private data were used.

papers.title: Accountable AI Delegation in Banking: Identity, Commitment Controls, Decision Evidence and Recovery
papers.abstract: An AI-assisted payment can pass assessment and lose release authority before commitment. We specify a banking delegation contract that checks current authority, the shared payment cap and the capacity of eligible instruments to cover losses. It books the new payment and its recovery demands and writes the outcome record in the same atomic transition. A paired example identifies the authorised mandate, applied rule and selection inputs a reviewer needs to assess mandate conformance. We show that, under fixed resource inputs, the transition preserves the payment cap and recovery feasibility when commitments and effective withdrawals are ordered against the same authoritative state. Reversing a transmitted priority changes the selected route in 4 of 32 distinct behavioural combinations, represented by 96 of 576 labelled contexts. The executor follows the transmitted rule in all of them. Reusing earlier state admits 23 releases in 123 histories blocked by the reference. Pooling recovery capacity admits 69 infeasible configurations in a grid of 576. Both current-state implementations agree with the reference in all 144 commitment histories and 624 concurrent schedules. The retention test recovers five specified outcome fields from each of 47 complete records. Fifteen survey responses informed requirements for resolving holds and handling uncertain delivery. An insurance example illustrates referral after an adverse coverage finding.

papers.title: The Assistant Persona Differs Across Languages in Activation Space
papers.abstract: Large language models behave differently across languages, and are noticeably less safe in lower-resource languages. This gap is well established behaviorally, but not mechanistically. Directions in activation space, including the assistant persona direction, are almost always extracted from English and assumed to generalize across languages. We extract the assistant persona direction in 31 languages in Qwen3-32B, and find that the resulting axes differ substantially: their cosine similarity to the English axis ranges from 0.378 to 0.911. Moreover, each language's assistant persona direction and its magnitude are correlated with the language's resource level. We also find that the model's default assistant state is farther from the helpful assistant pole in lower-resource languages. Finally, steering against a language's own axis amplifies persona-based jailbreak more than steering against the English axis. These results indicate that the model does not carry a single assistant representation across languages. More broadly, the assistant persona may need to be an explicit target of multilingual alignment.

papers.title: From Pilots to Position: Experimental Near-Field Localization for ISAC
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) enables wireless systems to reuse communication signals for environmental sensing, potentially reducing the need for dedicated sensing resources. However, the achievable localization accuracy of communication-centric waveforms under practical hardware constraints remains an important challenge. In this paper, we experimentally investigate near-field target localization using OFDM pilot signals in a distributed communication system. We consider both coherent and noncoherent localization approaches, exploiting multistatic propagation delays and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) information extracted from pilot-based channel estimates. A hardware setup comprising two transmitters and four receivers was developed and configured to operate at 3.4 GHz with 198 MHz occupied bandwidth to evaluate localization performance under realistic propagation and synchronization conditions. Experimental results across 16 static target positions demonstrate mean localization errors of 19.8 cm and 18.8 cm for coherent backprojection and noncoherent delay-TDOA fusion, respectively. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of occupied bandwidth on localization accuracy of the two proposed algorithms. These findings provide experimental insights into the capabilities and practical limitations of OFDM pilot-based sensing, supporting resource-efficient localization in future ISAC systems.

papers.title: Weighted fixed-bidegree subelliptic estimates for the \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on Lipschitz pseudoconvex domain
papers.abstract: We establish two types of \emph{a priori} subelliptic estimates for the twisted \(\overline{\partial}_f\)-Neumann problem on a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary. The estimates feature a subelliptic gain in \((0, 1/2)\) and are uniform with respect to the bidegree. The boundary is assumed to satisfy a plurisubharmonic-type condition, characterized by the local existence, near each boundary point, of a bounded plurisubharmonic function whose Hessian blows up algebraically near the boundary, with potentially different exponents at different points. The twisting function is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the domain, has bounded gradient, and its critical set inside the domain consists of isolated interior points with finite vanishing orders.

papers.title: Solar-Conditioned Flow Matching for Multitemporal Aerial Visible-to-Infrared Image Translation
papers.abstract: Aerial visible-to-infrared (V2IR) image translation provides scalable thermal data across the full diurnal cycle. However, existing methods predominantly learn a static mapping within narrow acquisition windows. As the thermal state evolves throughout the day, a single visible image may correspond to multiple plausible IR appearances, making V2IR translation an inherently multitemporal task. This letter proposes solar-conditioned latent flow matching (Solar-Flow), which upgrades aerial V2IR translation from static mapping to multitemporal generation. First, we design three computable physical factors, namely the solar elevation, the thermal phase clock (TPC), and the flight altitude. The TPC counts the elapsed heating and cooling hours on a continuous 24-hour axis anchored at sunrise, so the thermal state stays well defined even at hours without training samples. Second, we inject the condition into every Transformer block of a pretrained flow matching generator through adaptive layer normalization. This design preserves translation fidelity and enables multitemporal generation. Finally, we construct a paired aerial V2IR dataset covering 14 hour groups. Solar-Flow achieves multitemporal generation on this dataset, where a single visible image is translated into plausible IR images at multiple times of day, even at hours that were never seen in training.

papers.title: Turnout: Adaptive Attention Switching for Efficient Reasoning
papers.abstract: Post-hoc transformer linearization replaces the key-value cache of full attention, which grows linearly with generation length, with a fixed size state. This change reduces memory consumption but often hurts accuracy. In reasoning tasks, which require long generations, this effect is especially pronounced. In this work we introduce Turnout, a method that mitigates accuracy loss as a result of linearization, while maintaining its memory-reduction benefits. We apply post-hoc linearization to a pretrained full-attention model, training a linear path through distillation while leaving the original full-attention path unchanged. During response generation, the resulting hybrid model retains both paths and uses a learned policy to control when each layer switches from full to linear attention. We train the policy with reinforcement learning using a reward that balances answer correctness and memory use. Empirical evaluation of our method shows that the learned adaptive policy achieves a better accuracy-efficiency Pareto frontier on reasoning tasks compared to fixed switching and static hybrid baselines.

papers.title: NavRSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Vision-and-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have enabled vision-and-language navigation (VLN) through direct closed-loop perception and action. However, navigation performance depends strongly on the harness governing LLM-environment interactions, while existing harnesses largely rely on manually designed navigation tools, memory, and agent roles. We introduce NavRSI, a harness-centric recursive self-improvement framework that optimizes the navigation behavior of frozen LLMs through closed-loop experience. In each round, NavRSI iteratively collects navigation trajectories and failure diagnostics, employs a designer agent to rewrite the harness, and retains the revisions that prove effective, while the designer accumulates experience from previous revisions so that the harness and this experience co-evolve. Privileged simulator diagnostics guide only the designer and remain inaccessible to the navigating LLM, enabling deployment with a single RGB camera and primitive actions, without task-specific model training or additional navigation tools. Experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across LLMs from four vendors, with 85.64% success rate on the full R2R-CE val-unseen split with GPT-6-Astra, surpassing the previously reported best by 4.13%. Evaluations on RxR-CE, NavRAG-CE, and a real humanoid robot further demonstrate its generalizability.

papers.title: Solutions with one dimensional concentration for a two dimensional Schr\"odinger model with general potential and involving mass subcritical and supercritical exponents
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of solution $(\tilde u, \lambda)$ which concentrates on stationary and non-degenerate curve, as $p_\epsilon \to 6$, to the following mass-constraint nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation \begin{align*} \begin{cases} - \Delta \tilde u + W({\bf y}) \tilde u - |\tilde u|^{p_\epsilon-2} \tilde u = \lambda \tilde u, \quad {\bf y} \in \mathbb{R}^2, \\[2mm] \int_{\R^2} |\tilde u|^2 {\mathrm d} {\bf y} =a. \end{cases} \end{align*} Here $\lambda$ is a Lagrange multiplier, $ W({\bf y})$ is a real-valued potential, $a \in \mathbb{R}_+$ is a constant, $p_\epsilon = 6 \pm \epsilon, \epsilon \ll 1$ and $6$ is the $L^2$-critical exponent in the sense of concentration on a codimension 1 submanifold. When constructing the solution concentrating on a curve, we utilize some delicate transformations to overcome the challenges posed by the non-uniform boundedness of length of concentrating curves. In addition, we employ some refined analytical techniques to overcome the strong resonance phenomena caused by the $L^2$ constraint. Our result partially answers the Ambrosetti-Malchiodi-Ni conjecture in the setting of the mass-constrained nonlinear elliptic equation.

papers.title: Path-Aware Fusion of Infrastructure RF Sensing and Robot Perception in a Live Robotic Digital Twin
papers.abstract: Mobile robots in industrial workspaces must react to people that their onboard sensors cannot yet observe. Communication infrastructure can fill part of this gap by acting as a sensor, but its observations differ from camera and LiDAR evidence in meaning, spatial support, and rate. We present a live robotic Digital Twin (DT) that integrates heterogeneous sensing branches, a commodity 60-GHz link, joint Wi-Fi/5G sensing, a fixed camera, and robot-borne LiDAR, as spatially grounded observations with explicit freshness, and that uses the robot's live pose and heading to decide whether evidence lies on the path the robot is about to sweep. We show that a 60-GHz link carrying near-gigabit traffic detects human presence through the phase signature of its antenna array (balanced accuracy 0.98 on unseen sessions and 0.999 from one day to the next in a first site), but that a second site with a different link geometry requires a site-specific model (0.98 on unseen sessions after retraining, 0.73 without). On a Unitree Go2 patrolling under the DT, every person entering the camera field or the 60-GHz link stopped the robot (20/20); for the camera, the median time from physical entry to standstill was 1.83 s, of which detection, DT update, and networking take about 0.15 s and the rest is the 0.5-s confirmation and the robot's braking. Path-aware gating removed all stops caused by off-path presence (5 stops versus 0 for the same scenario), stale branches stopped the robot in fail-safe mode (6/6) and were ignored otherwise (0/6), and five unattended laps produced no false stop.

papers.title: Constraint-Aware Anticlustering Decomposition for Certifying Pairwise-Constrained Clustering
papers.abstract: Certifying the quality of feasible solutions to large-scale minimum sum-of-squares clustering with pairwise must-link and cannot-link constraints remains challenging, as it requires strong lower bounds on the optimal objective value. We propose a decomposition framework that partitions the data points into smaller subsets, called anticlusters, and solves the induced clustering subproblems to obtain a certified optimality gap for the original problem. To preserve pairwise information, we introduce the Constrained Anticlustering Problem (CAP), which assigns each connected component of the constraint graph to a single anticluster while seeking geometrically representative subsets. We formulate CAP as a mixed-integer second-order cone program and develop a variable neighborhood search heuristic to construct high-quality decompositions. The resulting lower bound remains valid even when the induced subproblems are not solved to global optimality. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets with up to approximately 4,000 observations show that our approach can achieve mean optimality gaps below 1% at a modest computational cost.

papers.title: Trained on Harm, Still Refusing: A Training-Time Defense for Code Generation
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning enables safety-aligned code language models to adapt to diverse downstream tasks. However, training on untrusted data can severely undermine their ability to refuse harmful requests. Notably, we find that models comply with harmful requests even though harmfulness information remains highly decodable from their internal representations. Moreover, an initial preference for refusal does not necessarily translate into sustained refusal behavior throughout generation. Together, these findings reveal a critical gap between recognizing harmful requests and consistently refusing to fulfill them. To address this gap, we introduce SAFEHOLD, a novel provider-enforced defense framework that preserves safety alignment during harmful fine-tuning by treating refusal as a sustained generation process rather than a single response decision. Specifically, SAFEHOLD preserves the aligned model's full-vocabulary response distribution at the initial generation position through decision-boundary anchoring, while supervising the complete refusal sequence through refusal-path reinforcement. We conduct extensive experiments evaluating safety, utility, and internal mechanisms. SAFEHOLD reduces average ASR by 72.03 percentage points relative to undefended fine-tuning, outperforming five SOTA defenses by 24.32 to 70.87 percentage points. Meanwhile, it improves average HumanEval pass@1 by 10.24 percentage points over undefended fine-tuning, while maintaining an average XSTest over-refusal rate of only 2.73 percent. Overall, these results demonstrate that SAFEHOLD effectively mitigates safety degradation during harmful fine-tuning while preserving benign-task utility.

papers.title: Typhoon OCR 2: From Thai Document Transcription to Multilingual, Multi-Task OCR
papers.abstract: Typhoon OCR 1.5 focused on reading Thai documents. However, in real-world workflows, users often need to extract specific information or preserve the structure of an entire page for further processing. Typhoon OCR 2 handles both tasks in a single model, with prompt-driven extraction and structured full-page parsing. Full-page parsing covers Thai, English, and Chinese. We release compact 2B and 0.8B models adapted from open document parsers through supervised fine-tuning on curated Thai and public multilingual data, followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task rewards and a rule penalizing unfinished responses. Among evaluated open models, Typhoon OCR 2 2B scores highest on Thai MDPBench (80.7 versus 68.9 for Typhoon OCR 1.5) and on ThaiOCRBench (59.91 versus 40.45), which covers recognition, extraction, and document understanding. The 2B model remains close to its base on English olmOCR-bench (84.7 versus 84.4) and on OmniDocBench, which evaluates English and Chinese together (90.97 versus 91.03). On MDPBench, GRPO reduces the mean share of pages with repetition loops for the 2B model from 3.2% to 0.7%, with a smaller and statistically uncertain score gain for the 0.8B model. We release the model weights, Python package, and evaluation suite.

papers.title: Global Critical $L^3$ Well-Posedness for the Stochastic Tamed Navier--Stokes Equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with Wiener and Jump Noise
papers.abstract: We study the global well-posedness for the three dimensional stochastic tamed Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with multiplicative Wiener and compensated Poisson noise. When noise coefficients are globally Lipschitz on $L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)$ and satisfy spatial $H^1_\sigma$ regularity assumptions, the system admits a pathwise unique global, probabilistically strong, critical mild solution for any initial datum $u_0 \in L^0(\Omega, \mathcal F_0; L^3_\sigma(\mathbb R^3)) $. Neither smallness nor moment or finite kinetic energy assumptions on $u_0$ are required. We also establish that the global solution depends continuously in probability on the initial datum in uniform-in-time $L^3$ and space-time $L^5$ norms on every finite time interval.

papers.title: Learning Unknown Oscillators From Bandit Feedback
papers.abstract: We study semi-bandits driven by unknown oscillators. Each round, a learner selects two of four reward channels and observes their individual rewards. Frequency errors change future reward rankings and the resulting measurements. We show when committing to one fitted oscillator lets its greedy choices expose prediction errors. Our controller bounds reward loss (regret) over a continuous confidence set and holds the longest block within budget. An online regression policy gathers observations when the check fails. Regret grows at a square-root rate, up to logarithmic factors, across all frequencies and extends to two competing oscillators. On 96 fresh synthetic instances, checked commitment uses 49 fits instead of 1,023, with 1.5% higher mean regret than fitting every round. Matched isolated timings give a 4.69-fold speedup. The confidence sets also certify trajectory regret.

papers.title: Alignment without Transfer: Tokenization Impacts Cross-lingual Representations during Multilingual Language Model Pretraining
papers.abstract: Tokenization represents one of the most crucial steps in mulilingual NLP pipelines. Yet, tokenizers routinely under-allocate vocabulary to low-resource languages. While improved allocation leads to better performance, it remains poorly understood how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations and transfer during pretraining. To address this, we pretrain 39 mono- and bilingual 1B decoder-only models on FineWeb2-HQ across English, German, French, Arabic and Chinese, varying only the tokenizer. Our results demonstrate that improved vocabulary allocation (i) substantially raises cross-lingual representation alignment in early-to-mid layers, an effect that prior work measuring only the output layer could not observe, (ii) increases cross-lingual parametric knowledge sharing in feed-forward neurons, supported by correlational and causal evidence, and (iii) an alignment-transfer dissociation, where cross-lingual transfer remains essentially unchanged despite higher alignment. Moreover, transfer is significantly lower for cross-script bilinguals even under fair vocabulary allocation, indicating that the script barrier is not merely a tokenizer artifact. All of our checkpoints and code are publicly available.

papers.title: Which Dwarf Is This? Doppeldwarf-306 and Near-Identical Instance Retrieval
papers.abstract: Most established instance-retrieval benchmarks emphasise landmarks; small sculptures from visually similar series offer a complementary challenge. We introduce Doppeldwarf-306: 1,691 openly licensed photographs of 306 bronze dwarf statues in Wroc{\l}aw, Poland, many made in themed series that share one style, with the photographer of each image recorded. With no training, nearest-neighbour search over frozen DINOv2 features names the right statue first for 93.1% of leave-one-out queries, and the best of thirteen backbones from seven pretraining paradigms reaches 94.7%. Accuracy falls slowly as candidates are added: for DINOv2, by about 0.8 points each time their number doubles. A natural design for a phone guide compares a photograph only with statues near the user. In simulation this helps, but less than an equal number of randomly chosen statues does, so random subsampling overstates its value; a permutation test ties the penalty to the real layout (p = 0.005). Used as a weight instead of a filter, location raises DINOv2 from 93.4% to 98.7% for a simulated user 25 m from the statue. With the query's photographer withheld, learned local-feature matching raises DINOv2 accuracy from 81.8% to 85.5% and also improves DINOv3. Comparing the two best candidates cuts DINOv2's false acceptance of unknown statues from 38.3% to 19.6% at 90% known acceptance.

papers.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
papers.abstract: Robots can be controlled to perform tasks with guaranteed correctness when the task instructions are stated in a formal language. Large language models (LLMs) have been widely used to allow users to provide such instructions in natural language (NL), by translating NL into formal language. When deploying such translators on a robot, however, we face limited computing and energy resources, while offloading computation or data to the cloud may be infeasible or undesirable. Yet an LLM is a general-purpose text generator, whereas a formula in a fixed formal language fragment follows a well-defined syntax. We therefore ask whether text generation is needed at all. For the formal language of linear temporal logic (LTL), we show that this translation can instead be broken down into answering a set of questions with pre-defined answers. We then construct a System-One model, a recent class of NL-based classifier, to provide such answers and enable us to translate a natural language instruction into an LTL instruction. On three benchmarks, our translator matches or exceeds the accuracy of the best local LLMs available, at up to one order of magnitude lower runtime and energy consumption. We show that it generalizes to unseen atomic propositions and temporal patterns.

papers.title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS fluxes. Deriving the BMS charges requires additional care, since BMS generators extended into the bulk are generally not tangent to the null hypersurfaces. After accounting for this and the associated anomalies, the renormalized canonical charges still contain an additional soft contribution. The prescription of a covariant boundary Lagrangian determines a corner improvement that removes this term and recovers the standard BMS charges.

papers.title: Verifying and Strengthening Neural Tangent Kernel Theory
papers.abstract: Writing Neural tangent kernel (NTK) theory explains why very wide neural networks trained by gradient methods converge in the lazy-training regime. Its standard proof combines matrix concentration, random Gram matrices, continuous-time dynamics, spectral perturbation, and a bootstrap argument, but has lacked machine-checked verification. We present a Lean\~4 formalisation for two-layer networks, proving an end-to-end theorem: for a smooth bounded activation (instantiated with $\sigma=\tanh$), frozen biases, paired $\pm 1$ initialisation, and explicit width conditions, gradient flow exists uniquely with probability at least $1-\delta$, and $$ \|r(t)\|^2 \leq \|y\|^2 e^{-\lambda_0 t/2}. $$ The sole data assumption is population NTK non-degeneracy, $\lambda_0>0$. Initial coercivity, kernel drift, the movement bootstrap, the residual ODE, and flow existence and uniqueness are formally proved. The formalisation also sharpens the standard analysis in two ways. First, replacing the conventional matrix-Bernstein variance proxy with the classical row-covariance proxy yields estimated concentration-width certificates for $\tanh$ that are $36$--$53\times$ smaller at $(m,d)=(16,8)$ and $94$--$121\times$ smaller at $(32,16)$. Lean certifies the inequality; the ratios are numerical. Second, the network Hessian has operator norm $\Theta(\sqrt{p})$ on the sup-norm parameter ball (a paper calculation), preventing the expected $O(1/\sqrt{p})$ linearisation bound via sup-norm Taylor estimates. An $L^2$ parameter geometry resolves this issue. Required widths remain polynomial but far beyond practical scales, limiting applicability.

papers.title: Practical insights into controlling exponential concentration in quantum machine learning
papers.abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models are often limited by exponential concentration, where quantum observables become insensitive to input variations as system size increases. In this work, we provide a comparative empirical study of this phenomenon across Fidelity Quantum Kernels (FQK), Projected Quantum Kernels (PQK), and Quantum Extreme Learning (QEL), within a unified observable-based framework based on expectation-value variance. We investigate how measurement locality, entanglement, and circuit expressivity shape concentration across different architectures. Global fidelity-based kernels exhibit strong concentration driven by Hilbert space dimensionality, whereas local-observable approaches reduce but do not eliminate this effect. In PQK and QEL, concentration is primarily governed by entanglement and quantum dynamical expressivity, with reservoir depth emerging as a key factor in QEL architectures. We further study bandwidth scaling as a general mechanism for controlling encoding expressivity across all models. Our results indicate that bandwidth scaling effectively reduces concentration in moderate regimes by restricting the effective expressivity of the encoding, though this protective effect diminishes in highly expressive structural settings.

papers.title: Risk sharing for background risk models with infinite mean
papers.abstract: Risk sharing is usually viewed as beneficial for risk-averse agents facing independent risks with finite means, but this situation can be reversed for infinite-mean losses. In this paper, we explore the effects of risk sharing for positively dependent infinite-mean losses using background risk models. Under both linear and conditional mean risk sharing, we show that risk sharing of infinite-mean losses can increase the risk in the sense of usual stochastic order. Our results cover classical multivariate loss distributions, including the Pareto-Clayton and the Fr\'echet-Gumbel models. For linear risk sharing, we further derive stochastic dominance relations between diversified portfolios, including those with Pareto marginals coupled by convex mixtures of commonly used Archimedean copulas. For conditional mean risk sharing, we additionally discuss peakedness and stochastic order relations for stable distributions. Consequently, under the stated conditions, retaining the original risk or a less diversified portfolio is preferred under every law-invariant monotone risk measure that is well defined for infinite-mean models.

papers.title: Boundary gradient asymptotics for superquadratic viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equations via optimal control
papers.abstract: We study the boundary behavior of the maximal solution of \[ -\Delta u + |\nabla u|^{p} + \lambda u = f \] on arbitrary bounded $C^{2}$ domains, where $p > 2$ and $\lambda > 0$. For bounded state-dependent terms $f$, we resolve a conjecture of Lasry and Lions by establishing sharp boundary gradient asymptotics without geometric restrictions on the domain. Previously, such asymptotics were established only for certain classes of domains with additional restrictions on $p$ and $f$. We also extend the analysis to state-dependent terms that may be singular near the boundary and obtain sharp boundary profiles and gradient asymptotics. Our approach relies on stochastic optimal control and boundary blow-up analysis. Dynamic programming estimates and comparisons of near-optimal trajectories establish tangential invariance of boundary blow-up limits, leading to the identification of one-dimensional profiles and the asymptotic formulas. For the associated state-constrained control problem, we establish sharp asymptotics for the minimizing feedback and deduce its admissibility and optimality, with corresponding results for the ergodic problem.

papers.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
papers.abstract: High expertise and cost barriers exclude small and medium-sized enterprises from discrete-event simulation (DES). We introduce GenAI4SimPy, a multi-agent framework powered by Qwen 3.6 (27B), an open-weight large language model, that automates end-to-end DES generation from manufacturing event logs to executable SimPy models through tool-augmented reasoning and human-in-the-loop validation. Evaluated on three execution blocks from a public smart factory dataset, the framework achieved a mean absolute percentage error of 7.9\% and coverage of failure rate for all three blocks and of throughput for two of three. A fidelity paradox was observed: accurate process-level parameters did not ensure system-level behavioral fidelity, with flow-time and throughput errors driven by misinterpreted observation-window truncation and absent system-level calibration. These results demonstrate that local open-weight models can perform DES generation at accuracy comparable to cloud-based alternatives, while identifying parameter extraction as necessary but insufficient for behavioral validity. Source code and results are available at https://github.com/RaikoPipe/genai4simpy

papers.title: Polarized IKKT holography: bulk realization of BPS operators
papers.abstract: We study the holographic imprint of polarization in the lowest BPS multiplet of the IKKT matrix model. On the matrix model side, the deformation requires operator mixing and broken-symmetry Ward identities to organize the surviving operators into an irreducible atypical multiplet of the $F(4)$ superalgebra. In the bulk, we use one-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity to identify the analytic half-BPS background with $F(4)$ symmetry whose boundary behavior matches the IKKT polarization. We solve the linearized bosonic and fermionic equations around this background and its undeformed counterpart exactly, and extract the independent asymptotic data. The supersymmetry transformations of these data reproduce the matrix model multiplets, thus establishing a bulk realization of this BPS operator structure.

papers.title: Scattering by two parallel semi--infinite arrays of sound--soft scatterers
papers.abstract: This article considers the scattering of an acoustic wave by two identical semi--infinite arrays of point scatterers which are positioned parallel to one another. The resulting system of scattering coefficients is formulated as a pair of coupled discrete Wiener--Hopf equations with a full $2\times2$ matrix kernel composed of two scalar kernel functions that represent interaction within the selected array and between the two arrays. Exploiting the symmetry of the two arrays, we introduce symmetric and antisymmetric components of the scattering coefficients, which decouple the matrix Wiener--Hopf system into two independent scalar problems with kernels given by the sum and difference of the two original kernel functions. The scalar Wiener--Hopf equations are then solved using the Wiener--Hopf technique in a very similar way to what has previously been used to solve the semi--infinite array problem. The original definitions of the two scalar kernels are represented by a lattice sum and practical evaluation techniques are discussed. Comparisons with previous work are also critically discussed. The resulting formulation provides an exact analytical solution to a coupled semi--infinite array problem and illustrates how symmetry can reduce a discrete matrix Wiener--Hopf problem to two scalar problems.

papers.title: Sprouting Fields of Conducting Polymer Dendrites as Evolving Organic Electrochemical Frameworks to Interconnect Electrode Arrays
papers.abstract: Balancing high performance with sustainability in microelectronics is challenged by energy-intensive processes, scarce materials and limited recyclability. Inspired by nature, a promising solution relies on the evolution of the foundry model to transient microelectronics, using electrochemistry to grow adaptive circuits on demand and during operation. To this end, this study explores how to harness the morphogenesis of conducting polymer dendrites between stacks of micro-electrode arrays to dynamically interconnect them with voltage pulses. Using propylene carbonate as a solvent, we investigated the dynamics of the electroconvective growth of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT), revealing strong structural dependencies between the morphology of the electrogenerated polymer and the confinement of the micro-electrodes. As the system evolves from 2D flat patterns to 3D dendritic structures, the capability of the conducting polymer to locally interconnect specific nodes heavily depends on the size and density of the arrays which directly impact the flow distribution during growth. By unraveling how a device geometry enables the growth of dendritic interconnections on integrated micro-electrode arrays, the morphogenesis of conducting polymer dendrites not only addresses the longstanding issue of heterogeneous integration in microelectronics, but also opens the way to a paradigm where electronic devices learn as they grow in our pockets.

papers.title: 3D-NAND-CIM: A Hybrid-Bonded 3D-NAND-Flash-based Analog In-Memory-Compute macro offering 4.8M weights/mm$^2$
papers.abstract: We describe an analog-in-memory-compute macro hybrid-bonding a 14nm logic die onto a 3D NAND Flash memory wafer, achieving weight density of 4.8M weights/mm$^2$. Weights are programmed to 1-of-16 conductances. MACs with current-controlled oscillator ADCs show weight-equivalent precision between 3 and 4 bits for 8-bit inputs on multiple NAND tiers at energy efficiencies up to 4.2 TOPS/W. A charge-retention circuit improves accuracy, with $\sim$0.4% (3.23%) accuracy drop on a WideResNet for CIFAR-10 (100).

papers.title: Transition processes of camphor particle motion in a three-chamber system
papers.abstract: The motion of a camphor particle in a chamber with three circular regions was investigated through experiments and numerical simulations. Transitions between circular regions were analyzed as discrete stochastic processes.
