This unavoidably makes model checking not easily accessible for researchers and engineers who may lack the required knowledge. Previous work has extended UML activity diagrams with probability and time, along with quality annotations, developed transformations from activity diagrams to probabilistic models which model checkers support, and implemented accompanying tools for automation. The research, however, is fragmented, informal, or not fully open, making its use, extension, and adaptation non-trivial. To mitigate these challenges, we introduce QANAD, a comprehensive verification framework for activity diagrams, that includes a new profile for probability, time, parameters, and quality annotations, a semantics interpretation of activity diagrams in Markov models variants (DTMCs, MDPs, and CTMCs) and their parametric versions, and a set of formal transformation rules from activity diagrams to the PRISM modelling language, supported by the leading model checkers PRISM and Storm. The theory underpinning QANAD has been realised into transformation implementation using model-driven engineering, enabling fully automated model transformation with automated verification using (parametric) probabilistic model checking and semi-automated synthesis. We demonstrate QANAD on a case study where multiple robots are used for delivery in a hospital environment and evaluated six other examples from the literature.

papers.title: Quotients of Leavitt path algebras over commutative rings by graded ideals
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a graph and $R$ a unital commutative ring. We study quotients of the Leavitt path algebra $L_R(E)$ by graded ideals which, unlike in the case of field coefficients, need not be basic. Using the saturated functions of Rigby and van den Hove, we introduce $I$-basic graded ideals, where $I$ is an ideal of $R$, and we prove that, for an arbitrary graph $E$, the quotient of $L_R(E)$ by an $I$-basic graded ideal is isomorphic to the Leavitt path algebra of a quotient graph of $E$ with coefficients in $R/I$. More precisely, for every graded ideal there is a canonical epimorphism from such an algebra onto the quotient, and it is an isomorphism if and only if the graded ideal is $I$-basic. This extends a result of Larki for basic graded ideals. We also introduce graded ideal functions, defined on the vertices of $E$ and on the pairs $(H,v)$ formed by a hereditary saturated set $H$ and a breaking vertex $v$ of $H$, and we show that they form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of graded ideals of $L_R(E)$. As an application, for a finite graph $E$ in which no cycle has an exit, we describe the quotient of $L_R(E)$ by any graded ideal as a direct sum, indexed by the sinks and the cycles of $E$, of Leavitt path algebras over quotient rings of $R$, namely matrix algebras over quotient rings of $R$ and of $R[x,x^{-1}]$. Finally, examples on the infinite binary tree and Toeplitz graph show that the hypothesis on the finiteness and cycles cannot be removed.

papers.title: Pseudo-random Instance Generators in C++ for Deterministic and Stochastic Multi-commodity Network Design Problems
papers.abstract: Network design problems constitute an important family of combinatorial optimization problems for which many exact and heuristic algorithms have been developed over the last few decades. Two central problems in this family are the multi-commodity, capacitated, fixed charge network design problem (MCFNDP) and its stochastic counterpart, the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP with recourse. These are standard problems that often serve as workbenches for devising and testing models and algorithms in stylized but near-realistic settings. Progress on solution methods requires instances of varying size, structure and difficulty. We present two open-source C++ generators. The deterministic generator modernizes and extends the generator underlying the Canad instances, with new topologies and continuous control of capacity tightness and cost structure. The stochastic generator, which is to our knowledge the first publicly available one for the two-stage stochastic MCFNDP, builds scenarios that match user-specified moments and correlations. We also release libraries of configurations for 6,000 deterministic and 416 stochastic instances, as well as the base instances and configurations of 20 stochastic instances on hub-and-spoke benchmark networks. The generators aim to support systematic and reproducible experimentation, including the training and out-of-sample evaluation of learning-based and stochastic programming methods.

papers.title: Odd Fredholm modules over differential graded algebras: Chern character and spectral flow
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a locally convex differential graded algebra. For $q \in \mathbb{N}_0$ we construct the Chern character of $\vartheta$-summable $\mathcal{C}_q$-Fredholm modules over $\Omega$, an entire cyclic cocycle which extends the JLO cocycle to the differential graded setting. For $q = 0$ it is the Chern character of even $\vartheta$-summable Fredholm modules over $\Omega$ due to G\"uneysu and Ludewig; for $q = 1$ it yields a Chern character for odd $\vartheta$-summable Fredholm modules over $\Omega$, which reduces to Getzler's odd Chern character for $\Omega$ trivially graded with trivial differential. We prove that this cocycle is Chen normalized and invariant under homotopies. Moreover, we generalize the constructions by Cacciatori and G\"uneysu to arbitrary $\Omega$ and $g \in \mathrm{GL}_m(\Omega^0)$ to get an odd chain $\mathrm{Ch}(g)$ and prove the following odd index theorem: the pairing of the odd Chern character with $\mathrm{Ch}(g)$ may be written as an explicit integral formula which equals $\sqrt{\pi}$ times the spectral flow from $Q$ to $\mathbf{c}(g)^{-1} Q \mathbf{c}(g)$ whenever $\mathbf{c}(g)$ is unitary. For odd-dimensional spin manifolds (where $\mathbf{c}$ is Clifford multiplication) this supplies the cochain side of the loop space approach to the odd-index theorem.

papers.title: Associativity conditions for linear quasigroups and equivalence relations on binary trees
papers.abstract: We characterise the bracketing identities satisfied by linear quasigroups with the help of certain equivalence relations on binary trees that are based on the left and right depths of the leaves modulo some integers. The numbers of equivalence classes of $n$-leaf binary trees are variants of the Catalan numbers, and they form the associative spectrum (a kind of measure of non-associativity) of a quasigroup. Every group-based equivalence relation arising here can be replaced by one defined by an abelian group generated by at most two elements. The fine associative spectra form a lattice isomorphic to the lattice of rank-two subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with an additional least element. This classifies the equivalence relations completely; closed formulas for all their numbers of classes remain open.

papers.title: OpinionGPT: Modelling Explicit Biases in Instruction-Tuned LLMs
papers.abstract: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently showcased remarkable ability to generate fitting responses to natural language instructions. However, an open research question concerns the inherent biases of trained models and their responses. For instance, if the data used to tune an LLM is dominantly written by persons with a specific political bias, we might expect generated answers to share this bias. Current research work seeks to de-bias such models, or suppress potentially biased answers. With this demonstration, we take a different view on biases in instruction-tuning: Rather than aiming to suppress them, we aim to make them explicit and transparent. To this end, we present OpinionGPT, a web demo in which users can ask questions and select all biases they wish to investigate. The demo will answer this question using a model fine-tuned on text representing each of the selected biases, allowing side-by-side comparison. To train the underlying model, we identified 11 different biases (political, geographic, gender, age) and derived an instruction-tuning corpus in which each answer was written by members of one of these demographics. This paper presents OpinionGPT, illustrates how we trained the bias-aware model and showcases the web application (available at https://opiniongpt.informatik.hu-berlin.de).

papers.title: Categorical concentration
papers.abstract: Given a torus action on a compact space $X$, a fundamental result of Borel and Atiyah-Segal asserts that the equivariant cohomology of $X$ is concentrated in the fixed locus $X^T$, up to inverting enough Chern classes. For algebraic varieties and stacks over an arbitrary field, we prove an analogous concentration statement for equivariant derived categories of sheaves. On the localized categories, restriction to the fixed locus coincides with Braden's hyperbolic localization, and as an application we obtain torus localization for the Donaldson-Thomas perverse sheaves of (-1)-shifted symplectic spaces. Concentration holds more generally for actions of affine algebraic groups, and for abstract six functor formalisms (e.g. motivic sheaves). For $\mu_\ell$-actions, it recovers Treumann's sheaf-theoretic Smith theory. We also prove a categorification of the virtual localization formula for torus actions.

papers.title: Euler characteristics and moderateness of Fujiki--Oka resolutions
papers.abstract: Fujiki--Oka resolutions of cyclic quotient singularities of type $\frac{1}{r}(1,a_2,\ldots,a_n)$ are constructed using multidimensional continued fractions. In this paper, we compute the Euler characteristics of Fujiki--Oka resolutions in arbitrary dimension using the heights of the coefficients of the associated remainder polynomials. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for moderateness of Fujiki--Oka resolutions in dimension three.

papers.title: Normative Ceilings and Stochastic Giving
papers.abstract: People randomize when they allocate money to others, and what else is available changes how they randomize: adding an alternative can raise the probability that an existing one is chosen, in violation of Regularity. We characterize a model of stochastic choice in which a selfish decision maker faces norm-driven social pressure and the menu matters only through one scalar, the normative ceiling, defined as the most pro-social alternative available. We introduce two conditions on cross-menu comparisons: comparisons line up through a single rescaling attached to each menu's most normative alternative, and higher normative levels are more selective. Together with standard positivity, continuity, acyclicity, order and richness requirements, these conditions force the randomization cost to depend on the menu only through the ceiling. Raising the ceiling makes the cost uniformly more curved. Random utility and baseline perturbed utility models imply Regularity; models of deliberate randomization necessarily violate it; ours does neither. Instead, our model predicts that Regularity can fail only when the ceiling rises across behaviorally distinguishable levels, and that it then fails at the least selfish alternatives. This prediction is a sign restriction with no free parameters, and we show how nested menus test it.

papers.title: Fitting height and lengths of laws in finite solvable groups
papers.abstract: Let G be a finite solvable group, and let h(G) denote its Fitting height, namely the length of a shortest normal series in G with nilpotent factors. We show, that h(G)/5 is a lower bound for the length of any law in G. It follows, that the cardinality of G is bounded from below by an exponential function of h(G). The proof is accomplished by showing an interesting result about the behaviour of non-trivial reduced words in permutation actions of finite solvable groups.

papers.title: Monodromy groups of Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an abelian variety over a number field. The connected monodromy field of $A$ is the minimal field over which the images of all the $\ell$-adic torsion representations have connected Zariski closure. We show that for all even $g \geq 4$, there exist infinitely many geometrically nonisogenous abelian varieties $A$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ of dimension $g$ where the connected monodromy field is strictly larger than the field of definition of the endomorphisms of $A$. Our construction arises from explicit families of hyperelliptic Jacobians with definite quaternionic multiplication.

papers.title: Structure theorem for cofibrant tame functors indexed by posets of dimension 1
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss certain circumstances in which the category of tame functors inherits an abelian category structure with minimal resolutions and a model category structure with minimal cofibrant replacements. We also present a structure theorem for cofibrant objects in the category of tame functors indexed by realizations of posets of dimension 1 with values in the category of chain complexes in an abelian category whose all objects are projectives. Moreover, we introduce a general technique to generate indecomposable objects in the abelian category of functors indexed by finite posets.

papers.title: Stratification de Hesselink rationnelle et contribution unipotente \`a la formule des traces en caract\'eristique p>0
papers.abstract: For a field $F$ and a connected reductive group $G$ defined over $F$, we develop a theory of Kempf-Rousseau-Hesselink unipotent $F$-strata in $G(F)$ that should allow us to attack open problems in positive characteristic. As an application, we use this theory to establish an expansion (preliminary to the fine expansion) of the unipotent contribution to the trace formula over a global field of characteristic $p>0$. The unipotent $F$-strata play here the role of the unipotent geometric orbits in Arthur's work over a number field. The expansion in terms of products of local distributions is not discussed here; it will be the subject of further work.

papers.title: The Stochastic Arrival Problem
papers.abstract: We study a new modification of the Arrival problem, which allows for nodes that exhibit random as well as controlled behaviour, in addition to switching nodes. We study the computational complexity of these extensions, building on existing work on Reachability Switching Games. In particular, we show for versions of the arrival problem involving just switching and random nodes it is \PP{}-hard to decide if their value is greater than a half and we give a PSPACE decision algorithm.

papers.title: The homotopy types of $Sp(n)$-gauge groups over $S^{4m}$
papers.abstract: Let $m$ and $n$ be two positive integers such that $m < n$. Denote by $P_{n,k}$ the principal $Sp(n)$-bundle over $S^{4m}$ and $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$ be the gauge group of $P_{n,k}$ classified by $k\varepsilon'$, where $\varepsilon'$ is a generator of $\pi_{4m}(B(Sp(n)))\cong\mathbb{Z}$. In this article, we will partially classify the homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$ by giving a lower bound for the number of homotopy types of $\mathcal{G}_{k,m}(Sp(n))$. Also, in special cases $Sp(3)$-gauge groups over $S^8$ and $Sp(4)$-gauge groups over $S^{12}$ we give an upper bound for the number of homotopy types of these gauge groups.

papers.title: Where the Model Frequently Meets the Road: Combining Statistical, Formal, and Case Study Methods
papers.abstract: This paper briefly analyzes the working or default assumptions researchers in the formal, statistical, and case study traditions typically hold regarding the sources of unexplained variance, parameter values, functional forms, time, and external validity. We argue that these working assumptions are often not essential to each method, and that these assumptions can be relaxed in ways that allow multimethod work to proceed. We then analyze the comparative advantages of different combinations of formal, statistical, and case study methods, and offer advice on how to combine these methods.

papers.title: On the Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for multi-layer ResNets in the mean-field regime
papers.abstract: Finding the optimal configuration of parameters in ResNet is a nonconvex minimization problem, but first-order methods often find the global optimum when the network is overparameterized and the training algorithm is run for sufficiently many iterations. We study this phenomenon in the mean-field regime, where the network can be described approximately by an ordinary integral equation (OIE) and the training process of ResNet becomes a gradient-flow partial differential equation (PDE). Under the condition that the activation function is $2$-homogeneous or partially $1$-homogeneous, we show that this gradient-flow PDE converges to the global minimum. This result suggests that if the ResNet is sufficiently large, first-order optimization methods can find global minimizers that fit the training data as well. Further, by controlling the generalization error, we prove that the gradient-flow PDE is stable with respect to its cost function, implying that a finite-sized but sufficiently large dataset drawn from the underlying data distribution can exhibit the properties of the continuous limit. We give lower bounds on the depth and width of the network for the gradient-flow approximation to hold. We also lower-bound the size of the training data set needed to attain accurate approximation.

papers.title: Harmonic mean closed vector lattices
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of the harmonic mean on certain Archimedean vector lattices, which we call harmonic mean closed. Using this concept, we provide a new characterization of positive orthogonally additive polynomials from a harmonic mean closed Archimedean vector lattice to a uniformly complete Archimedean vector lattice space entirely in terms of harmonic means. This result yields polynomial versions of the QM-AM-GM-HM inequalities on Archimedean vector lattices where the only additional requirement on the domain space is that it is harmonic mean closed.

papers.title: A Certified Reduced Basis Method for Linear Parametrized Parabolic Optimal Control Problems in Space-Time Formulation
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose to efficiently solve time dependent parametrized optimal control problems governed by parabolic partial differential equations through the certified reduced basis method. In particular, we will exploit an error estimator procedure, based on easy-to-compute quantities which guarantees a rigorous and efficient bound for the error of the involved variables. First, we propose analyzing the problem at hand, proving its well-posedness thanks to Ne\v cas - Babu\v ska theory in a space-time formulation. Then, we derive error estimators to apply a Greedy method during the offline stage, to perform, during the online stage, a Galerkin projection onto a low-dimensional space spanned by properly chosen high-fidelity solutions. We tested the error estimators on two model problems governed by a Graetz flow with physical and geometrical parametrization. The results have been compared to a previously proposed bound, based on the exact computation of the Babu\v ska inf-sup constant, in terms of reliability and computational costs. We remark that our findings still hold in the steady setting, and we also propose a brief insight for this simpler formulation.

papers.title: Space-Efficient Interior Point Method, with applications to Linear Programming and Maximum Weight Bipartite Matching
papers.abstract: We study the problem of solving linear programs in the streaming model. Given a constraint matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and vectors $b\in\mathbb{R}^m, c\in\mathbb{R}^n$, we develop a space-efficient interior point method that optimizes solely on the dual program. To this end, we obtain efficient algorithms for various different problems. For general linear programs whose feasible region lies in a ball of radius $R$ and contains a ball of radius $r$ with known center, we can solve them in $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{n}\log(mR^2\|c\|_2/(r\epsilon)))$ passes and $\widetilde{O}(n^2)$ space for an $\epsilon$-approximate solution. To the best of our knowledge, this is the most efficient LP solver in streaming with no polynomial dependence on $m$ for both space and passes. For bipartite graphs, we can solve the minimum vertex cover and maximum weight matching problems (with polynomially bounded integer weights) in $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{m})$ passes and $\widetilde{O}(n)$ space. In addition to our space-efficient IPM, we also give algorithms for solving SDD systems and the isolation lemma in $\widetilde{O}(n)$ space, which are the cornerstones for our graph results.

papers.title: Small scale quantum ergodicity in cat maps
papers.abstract: We study small scale quantum ergodicity in quantum cat maps, with semiclassical parameter 1/N, and prove three groups of results. First, for every N and every eigenbasis, almost all eigenstates are equidistributed on phase space balls of radius (log N)^(-a) for a 1/2 in phase space and a>1 in position space. Hence, the exponents 1/2 and 1 in the first group are sharp: even for a full density subset of eigenstates, quantum ergodicity at fixed scales does not extend beyond the critical logarithmic scales.

papers.title: Lofty Models of Peano Arithmetic
papers.abstract: If M is a nonstandard model of Peano Arithmetic, then M is lofty iff M has a simple elementary extension that is recursively saturated. This had previously been known for countable M.

papers.title: Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs
papers.abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the probability that the simple random walk on a vertex-transitive graph escapes the ball of radius $r$ before returning to its starting point. In particular, this shows that if the ball of radius $r$ has size slightly greater than quadratic in $r$ then this probability is bounded from below. On the other hand, we show that if the ball of radius $r$ has volume slightly less than cubic in $r$ then this probability decays logarithmically for all larger balls. These results represent a finitary refinement of Varopoulos's theorem that a random walk on a vertex-transitive graph is recurrent if and only if the graph has at most quadratic volume growth. They also imply the existence of a gap at $0$ for escape probabilities: there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that the random walk on an arbitrary vertex-transitive graph is either recurrent or has a probability of at least $c$ of escaping to infinity. We also prove versions of these results for finite graphs, in particular confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Benjamini and Kozma from 2002. Amongst other things, we also generalise our results to give a sharp finitary version of the characterisation of $p$-parabolic vertex-transitive graphs, prove a number of sharp isoperimetric inequalities for vertex-transitive graphs, and prove a locality result for the escape probability of the random walk on a vertex-transitive graph that can be seen as an analogue of Schramm's locality conjecture for the critical percolation probability.

papers.title: Revisiting the Graph Isomorphism Problem with Semidefinite Programming
papers.abstract: It is well-known that two graphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ on $n$ vertices are isomorphic if and only if their compatibility graph, an auxiliary graph on $n^2$ vertices, contains a clique of order $n$. In this paper, we give an exact conic formulation of this clique problem. We show that $G_1$ and $G_2$ are isomorphic if and only if a system of linear constraints over the cone of completely positive matrices is feasible. Since deciding membership in the completely positive cone is NP-hard, this formulation does not by itself yield an efficient algorithm. Relaxing complete positivity to positive semidefiniteness yields a semidefinite program whose infeasibility certifies that the two graphs are not isomorphic. We establish basic properties of this relaxation. Specifically, it is at least as strong as the necessary condition given by the Lov\'asz $\vartheta$ number of the complement of the compatibility graph, it never admits a strictly feasible solution, and it is implied by the degree-two level of the Lasserre hierarchy applied to a natural integer formulation of graph isomorphism. In light of known lower bounds for the Lasserre hierarchy, the latter indicates that the relaxation cannot decide isomorphism for all pairs of graphs. We leave open the question of characterizing the pairs of graphs for which the relaxation is tight.

papers.title: An Open Petri Net Implementation of Gene Regulatory Networks
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are a central object of systems biology, and many formalisms have been used to model them, among them Petri nets. Ordinary Petri nets, however, provide no built-in way to assemble a large network from smaller, separately specified pieces. Open Petri nets, in the sense of Baez and Master, supply exactly this: an open Petri net is a Petri net with designated boundary places, and open Petri nets are composed by gluing boundaries together (a pushout), giving a symmetric monoidal double category Open(Petri). In this paper we (i) state precisely the standard encoding of activation, inhibition and degradation as Petri net transitions; (ii) distinguish the classical "Petri nets are monoids" view of Meseguer and Montanari, which describes how processes inside one net compose, from the open Petri net view, which describes how nets compose; (iii) show, with a worked example, how a GRN can be cut into open Petri net modules along shared genes and recovered exactly by composition, together with simple rules that make such a decomposition correct; and (iv) use the compositional rate-equation semantics of Baez and Pollard to show that the mass-action dynamics of the composite network are obtained by gluing the dynamics of its modules, linking Petri net models of GRNs to their ordinary differential equation counterparts. We close by discussing what the reachability semantics does and does not give for GRN modules, and the limitations of the approach.

papers.title: On the interplay between noise and curvature and its effect on optimization and generalization
papers.abstract: The speed at which one can minimize an expected loss using stochastic methods depends on two properties: the curvature of the loss and the variance of the gradients. While most previous works focus on one or the other of these properties, we explore how their interaction affects optimization speed. Further, as the ultimate goal is good generalization performance, we clarify how both curvature and noise are relevant to properly estimate the generalization gap. Realizing that the limitations of some existing works stems from a confusion between these matrices, we also clarify the distinction between the Fisher matrix, the Hessian, and the covariance matrix of the gradients.

papers.title: A Categorical Compositional Distributional Modelling for the Language of Life
papers.abstract: The Categorical Compositional Distributional (DisCoCat) model is a mathematical framework for computing the meaning of a sentence from the meanings of its words and the grammatical structure that combines them. Because biological sequences can be viewed as a "language of life", it is tempting to ask whether the DisCoCat model can also give insight into biological macromolecules. Here we take a first step in this direction for proteins, whose linguistic features are the most prominent among the macromolecules. We treat a protein as a sentence and its domains as words, take the biological function of a domain or protein as its meaning, and regard the arrangement of domains as the syntax. We give pregroup grammar types to protein domains and to the linker regions between them, show how type reductions are lifted to multilinear maps between vector spaces, and use these maps to compute a vector representation of a protein's function from vector representations of its domains. In particular, linkers act as relational "words" whose order-three tensors combine the two flanking domains into a vector in a single protein meaning space, so that the functions of proteins with different domain architectures can be compared by an inner product. We extend the construction to proteins with any number of domains, illustrate it with a numerical toy example and five Drosophila melanogaster proteins, discuss how the linker tensors could be learned and how the model could be tested, and relate it to protein language models and other developments since 2019.

papers.title: Unitarizability of weight modules over noncommutative Kleinian fiber products
papers.abstract: Noncommutative Kleinian fiber products $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ are $\ast$-algebras attached to $(m,n)$-periodic higher spin six-vertex configurations $\mathscr{L}$. Examples include quotients of the enveloping algebra of the affine Lie algebra $A_1^{(1)}$ and of a finite W-algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_4$. We determine which simple integral weight $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$-modules carry an invariant inner product and which of them are unitarizable, and we compute the signature of the form. All three answers are read off from the vertex configuration: the signature of a module is a count of faces in a two-coloring of an eight-vertex configuration canonically attached to $\mathscr{L}$. The main tool is a one-parameter family $\Delta_\xi$ of representations of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ by difference operators on sections of a line bundle over the face lattice. These representations carry an explicit indefinite invariant inner product, and together they contain every simple integral weight module. Along the way we show that the Casimir element of $\mathcal{A}(\mathscr{L})$ is unitary.

papers.title: $L^p-L^q$ estimates for maximal operators associated to families of finite type curves
papers.abstract: We investigate the \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) boundedness of maximal operators associated with averages over families of finite-type curves in the plane. These operators are defined by \[ \mathbb{M}f(x):=\sup_{1\leq t\leq 2} \left|\int_{\mathbb{C}}f(x-ty)\rho(y)\,d\sigma(y)\right|, \] where \(d\sigma\) denotes the normalized Lebesgue measure on the curve \(\mathbb{C}\), and \(\rho\) is a smooth cutoff function. Let \(\triangle\) denote the closed triangle with vertices \[ P=\left(\frac25,\frac15\right),\qquad Q=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right),\qquad R=(0,0). \] We establish that, whenever \[ \left(\frac1p,\frac1q\right) \in \bigl(\triangle\setminus\{P,Q\}\bigr) \cap \left\{ \left(\frac1p,\frac1q\right): \frac1p \frac{(m+1)q}{q+1} \right\}, \] there exists a constant \(B>0\) such that \[ \|\mathbb{M}f\|_{L^q(\mathbb{R}^2)} \leq B\|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb{R}^2)}. \] As an application, we derive \(L^p\)-\(L^q\) estimates for solutions of higher-order strictly hyperbolic pseudodifferential equations.

papers.title: Hypercube LSH for approximate near neighbors
papers.abstract: A celebrated technique for finding near neighbors for the angular distance involves using a set of random hyperplanes to partition the space into hash regions [Charikar, STOC 2002]. Experiments later showed that using a set of orthogonal hyperplanes, thereby partitioning the space into the Voronoi regions induced by a hypercube, leads to even better results [Terasawa and Tanaka, WADS 2007]. However, no theoretical explanation for this improvement was ever given, and it remained unclear how the resulting hypercube hash method scales in high dimensions. In this work, we provide explicit asymptotics for the collision probabilities when using hypercubes to partition the space. Vectors at angle $\pi/3$ collide with probability $(\sqrt{3}/\pi)^{d + o(d)}$ in dimension $d$, compared to $(2/3)^d$ for random hyperplanes, and near-parallel vectors collide with similar asymptotic probabilities in both cases. The limiting exponential base tends continuously to zero as the angle approaches $\frac{\pi}{2}$ from below. For fixed near and far angular thresholds below $\pi/2$, these asymptotics determine the limiting LSH collision-probability ratio $\rho$. We further describe how to use hypercube LSH in practice. A direct partial-hypercube analysis gives a heuristic lattice-sieving time bound $2^{0.3347d+o(d)}$.

papers.title: Non-Abelian Quantum Turbulence in Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensates
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate statistically steady quantum turbulence in the cyclic phase of a spin-2 spinor Bose--Einstein condensate (BEC) driven by large-scale energy injection via a divergence-free external velocity field. In the full non-Abelian cyclic system, the mass-current spectrum exhibits an anomalous $k^{-7/3}$ scaling, whereas the spin-current spectrum approximately follows a $k^{-5/3}$ power law. To isolate the role of non-Abelian vortex dynamics, we compare this system with an Abelian-restricted cyclic system sharing the same Hamiltonian parameters and driving conditions. Strikingly, the Abelian restriction collapses both the mass- and spin-current spectra into a single $k^{-5/3}$ scaling, identical to that of a scalar BEC, despite the three distinct turbulent states maintaining nearly identical vortex-line densities. A Helmholtz decomposition reveals that the mass- and spin-current spectra are predominantly incompressible and transverse, respectively, thereby confirming that the anomalous scaling cannot be attributed simply to compressible fluctuations or to the transverse nature of the energy injection. Local spectral exponents further quantify these distinct scaling regimes. The disappearance of the mass-spin spectral separation under the Abelian restriction, alongside the formation of a large-scale web of rung-connected non-Abelian vortices, provides compelling evidence that non-Abelian vortex dynamics fundamentally govern the organization of turbulent mass flow.
